newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania Democrats claim landslide win in polls.
newsitem.headline: Albania Democrats claim landslide win in polls.

text.p: Albania's ruling Democrats claimed on Monday they had won most of the city halls and communes at stake in a run-off ballot on Sunday, confirming the party's landslide victory in local elections.

"Sunday's run-off round was a complete victory for the Democratic Party on all levels," party leader Tritan Shehu told a news conference. "The general electoral geography speaks everywhere for the Democratic Party."

The Democrats said preliminary results showed they had gained a majority in 21 out of 22 city halls and 73 out of 96 communes. Overall the Democrats won 90.6 percent of the city halls and 86.7 percent of the communes, Shebu said.

He said the opposition Socialists, the reformed heirs to the communists, gained only 6.25 percent of the city halls and 4.5 percent of the communes, down from 51 percent and 59.8 percent respectively at the last elections in 1992.
Turnout was about 72 percent of the electorate, eight percent more than in 1992. Official results are due later in the week.
The Socialists have criticised the way the elections were conducted, but the Council of Europe, which monitored the polls, said initial findings suggested there were no serious irregularities.
General elections in Albania in May and June ended in controversy when most opposition parties, including the Socialists, withdrew, alleging the ballot was rigged.
